_comment: jshe scenario - CIMD Agent Governance leg against a third-party participant: Descope as the CIMD-capable AS, a Cloudflare Workers MCP server (Minority Prophet OpenID AIIM Interop Referee) as the resource. Like 11AIBlockchain this points Client:Server:Endpoint at an external server (so there is no Server-side profile), but registration is CIMD (UseCimd=true), not a pre-registered client. Confirmed working end-to-end 2026-09-08/13 against an earlier config (tunnel-hosted CIMD doc, CimdAuthMethod=none, tunnel-hosted RedirectUri) - superseded 2026-09-27 by CimdDocumentUrl pointing at the repo's published GitHub Pages doc instead (see appsettings.GitHubPages.json, .github/workflows/publish-cimd.yml), which forces CimdAuthMethod=private_key_jwt (the new default) and a RedirectUri that matches the published doc's redirect_uris character for character (CimdDocumentFactoryTests guards this) - currently https://127.0.0.1:5050/callback, no tunnel needed for the CIMD document anymore. NOT yet re-confirmed end-to-end against Descope with this pairing - the earlier 'Descope silently stalls on a loopback redirect for a CIMD client' finding was observed under the superseded tunnel+none-auth setup, so treat it as untested here rather than assuming it still applies. If Descope does stall/reject on this loopback redirect, the fix is republishing cimd/client-metadata.json + cimd/jwks.json with a different RedirectUri (regenerate via the GitHubPages scenario's generation path, push to main to trigger the publish workflow), not editing this file alone - CimdDocumentUrl and RedirectUri must always match what's actually published. Authority is the Descope issuer (discovery URL minus /.well-known/openid-configuration) - optional for CIMD, kept as the AuthServerSelector safety net. No Ema section: UseEma is false. No Client:Resource: Descope binds the MCP endpoint into the access token's aud from its own app config without an RFC 8707 resource indicator, so the SDK 2.0.0 gap does not matter here. Scopes stays [ "mcp:tools" ] (an empty array here is a silent no-op per .NET config binding - see ClientOptions.Scopes/ForceEmptyScope docs, do not use it to try to suppress the scope request) - the ScopeSelector in Endpoints.cs also now intersects whatever the challenge/PRM advertise with this list, so a resource server offering an unwanted scope (confirmed: this referee's rotating canary:challenge:<date>/canary:oprm:<date> probe scope) never gets echoed back. ForceEmptyScope=false: confirmed 2026-09-13 that Descope grants the inbound app's configured mcp:tools scope regardless of what scope the client requests, so the participant's missing-scope negative case is not reachable from the client side at all - set to true only to reproduce/re-verify that finding, not to expect a different token.
